fixes.explanation: Muddy sounds believable, but it's not what God says. He tells Moses the Israelites will go through the sea “…on dry ground.” (Exodus 14:16) Verses 22 and 29 say it again, with walls of water on both sides. Muddy would have meant a whole nation losing their sandals in the muck, and the text never has that problem. I think I'd have kept checking my feet the whole way across.

An earthquake is a big, dramatic guess, and I respect the drama. But the text says the LORD drove the sea back “…with a strong east wind…” (Exodus 14:21), and it blew all that night. No rumbling, no shaking, just wind doing steady work for hours. I once stood in front of an oven door that wouldn't stop blowing hot air, and I still wouldn't call that an earthquake.
